newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends tad up after two-way trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends tad up after two-way trade.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended a shade up on Monday from New York's Friday close after two-way trade, but the market traded within a a tight range with scarce activity during a public holiday in Japan, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$368.40/90 an ounce on Monday against New York's US$368.30/80 close on Friday.
"Some early selling out of Australia was countered by local physical buying," a gold dealer said.
Europe opened a tad firmer on light buying, dealers said.

Gold traded between $368.40 and $368.70 during Hong Kong business hours and was marked by a lack of trading interest prior to the Christmas holiday and during a public holiday in Japan, another trader said.
Local gold ended HK$4 lower at HK$3,404 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -6.00 from its previous fix at -0.10.
